object.attr: as implemented: mapped from the existing tests, with blind tests written from the requirements alone for what they missed.
object.description: For each kind of validation error that release 0.3.0 reported, make a document with a problem of that kind, validate it and read the codes: an attribute the manifest doesn't define (ATTR_UNKNOWN); a required attribute not set (ATTR_MISSING_REQUIRED); an enumeration value that isn't an option (ATTR_BAD_ENUM); integer values abc and 3.14 (ATTR_BAD_INTEGER); real values abc and 1.2.3 (ATTR_BAD_REAL); boolean values yes and True (ATTR_BAD_BOOLEAN); date values 25/04/2026 and not-a-date (ATTR_BAD_DATE); an outline that names one object twice (OUTLINE_DUP); an outline entry whose object doesn't exist (OUTLINE_MISSING_OBJECT); an object that isn't in the outline (OBJECT_NOT_IN_OUTLINE); a link to a document that isn't a parent document (LINK_NOT_ALLOWED); a link to an object ID of the same document that no object has (LINK_TARGET_MISSING); the metadata date 2026-04-215 (META_BAD_DATE); a rule that requires an attribute the object lacks (RULE_REQUIRED_MISSING), one that forbids an attribute the object has (RULE_FORBIDDEN_PRESENT), and one that requires a link to a parent document the object doesn't have (RULE_LINK_REQUIRED_MISSING). Expected: each document reports the code in brackets, which is the code release 0.3.0 used for that kind, and the two values tried for one kind give the same code.
